headline: Fee earnings grow double digits on strong fundraising
summary_short: Fee-related earnings were $864M, up 15% y/y, and distributable earnings were $763M ($0.47/share), also up 15%. BAM raised $25B in the quarter and $123B year to date.
summary_long: Fee-bearing capital reached $682B, up 13% y/y, helped by $157B raised over twelve months. BAM invested $18B and monetized $12B in the quarter, and realized $48M of net carried interest for the first time since spinout. Net income of $3.0B includes a non-cash gain tied to consolidating Oaktree. Uncalled fund commitments were $148B and corporate liquidity was $2.1B. The board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.5025 per share.
confidence_notes: Release states results reflect a new presentation for partner managers; prior periods are recast and FRE, DE and net income are unaffected. Net income includes a non-cash gain on the Oaktree acquisition and consolidation. FRE and DE are non-GAAP. y/y deltas computed from the release's own current and prior-year figures.

drivers.explanation: Management says fee-bearing capital growth of 13% over the past year, driven by capital inflows and strong deployment, drove fee-related earnings higher.
Growth was driven largely by the $157B raised over the last twelve months, with broad-based strength across the franchise.
The release cites a $2.0B non-cash gain on the acquisition and consolidation of Oaktree, which lifts net income well above fee earnings.
Infrastructure drew roughly $50B of commitments over the past year, private equity raised $14B at a record pace, and credit raised $12B in the quarter.
